Kovel Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is Kovel's oldest Jewish cemetery, historically called 'yashan noshan' (the oldest one), believed to have emerged in the late 16th century; per Kovel's own Yizkor memorial book, a tombstone dated 1611 was recorded there in the 1930s. Jews settled in Kovel from the early 16th century, gaining the right to reside on all streets in 1614; Rabbi Mordechai of Neskhizh's relocation from Toykut, documented elsewhere in this collection, brought Trisk, Neskhizh, and Ruzhin Hasidism to the city. The Jewish population reached 8,521 by 1897 and 12,758 by 1921; noted politician Chaim Pazner (1899–1981) was a resident. Following the June 1941 occupation, two ghettos held about 24,000 Jews, with 8,600 murdered in a single action on June 3–5, 1942. This cemetery was most likely demolished during WWII; a local school now occupies part of the site, its principal reportedly unaware a Jewish cemetery ever stood there.
